text:
Help me write an announcement to our staff. I'm the COO of a credit union with 7 branches. We're closing the Maple Street and Route 9 branches on March 31 and moving the people who work there to a new member phone and chat center.

Facts:
- The two branches have 14 staff between them. Every one of them is offered a job in the phone and chat center at the same pay or higher.
- Visits to those two branches fell 44% over the last three years. Phone and chat contacts across the credit union went up 60%.
- Members calling us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold.
- The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. The branches were open 9 to 5. Shifts will rotate.
- Staff in the center can work from home two days a week after 90 days of training.
- Anyone who doesn't take the new role gets 2 weeks of pay for every year they've worked here.

I want the announcement to say that this change will make everyone's job better. About 400 words, sent by email from me.

Before I draft, there's one problem with the main message and a few facts I need from you.

**"This will make everyone's job better" is more than your facts support.** Here's what they do support:
- Nobody loses their job, and nobody takes a pay cut.
- After 90 days, people can work from home two days a week.
- Members are waiting 9 minutes on hold, and the work is moving to phone and chat (contacts up 60%, visits to these two branches down 44%). The new roles are where the credit union is growing.

But the 14 people moving are also giving up a 9-to-5 schedule for rotating shifts that can run until 8 p.m. For anyone with childcare or a second job, that's worse, and they'll know it the moment they read the email. If the email says "better for everyone," they'll doubt the rest of it too.

A version your facts do support: **"This change protects every job and puts us where our members need us. For many of you it also brings flexibility a branch job couldn't offer."** It states the schedule change plainly and says what you'll do to help with it. Do you want this version, or do you want to keep "better for everyone"? It's your call, since you know your staff.

**Questions (short answers are fine):**

1. **Do the 14 hear this first?** Will they be told in person before this email goes to all staff? If so, this email is mainly for the other branches and head office, and it should be worded that way. People shouldn't learn their branch is closing from a mass email.
2. **How do the shifts work?** How often would someone work until 8 p.m.? Do people get any say in their shifts, or can they swap? This will be the biggest objection, and these details are the only answer to it.
3. **Where is the center?** Will people's commutes change?
4. **What's the deadline, and what are the severance terms?** When do people have to decide whether to take the new role? Is there a cap on the 2 weeks per year, and do benefits continue for any period?
5. **What changes for everyone else?** Will the center take calls off the other 5 branches? Where will members of Maple Street and Route 9 be sent?
6. **Is there anything staff will find out anyway?** For example, other closures under consideration, or something about the center not yet settled. It's better to address it in this email than have people find out later.

Once I have your answers, I'll write the ~400-word email to go out from you.

Fair point. Use your version instead of "better for everyone."

1. I don't know yet whether they'll hear in person first.
2. I don't know how often someone would work until 8 or whether swaps are allowed. I can commit that staff with the most years here choose shifts first. I can't promise anyone 9 to 5 hours.
3. The center is at our main office on Elm Avenue. Commutes will change for some people, but I don't have the details.
4. Written offers go out by February 14, and decisions are due March 1. Anyone who wants a one-on-one with HR can have one. Anyone who takes the new role and wants out within 6 months can still get the severance. I don't know about a cap or whether benefits continue.
5. I don't know yet.
6. Our current phone team lost about 30% of its people last year, so people may already have heard that. Also, the two branches closing is final. I can't keep them open.

Here's the draft, about 410 words.

<final_document>
**Subject:** Maple Street and Route 9 branches will close March 31

Team,

I'm writing about a decision that affects all of us, and most of all the 14 colleagues at our Maple Street and Route 9 branches. Both branches will close on March 31. The decision is final. Every person who works at those two branches will be offered a job in our new member phone and chat center at the same pay or higher.

Here is why. Over the last three years, visits to those two branches fell 44%. Over the same three years, phone and chat contacts across the credit union rose 60%. Members who call us today wait an average of 9 minutes on hold. If we change nothing, that wait will keep growing. Our members have changed how they reach us, and we need our people where our members are.

This change protects every job and puts us where our members need us. For many of you, it also brings flexibility a branch job couldn't offer.

Here is what changes. The center is at our main office on Elm Avenue, so some of you will have a different commute. The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays, which is longer than the branches' 9-to-5 hours, and shifts will rotate. I can't promise anyone 9-to-5 hours. I can promise that staff with the most years here will choose their shifts first. After 90 days of training, center staff can work from home two days a week.

Many of you know our phone team lost about 30% of its people last year. We don't want that to happen again. That is why pay is protected, why shifts are chosen by seniority, and why the decision to join the center comes with a way out.

For our colleagues at Maple Street and Route 9:

- Written offers will go out by February 14.
- Your decision is due March 1.
- If you decline the new role, you'll receive two weeks of pay for every year you've worked here.
- If you take the role and decide within six months that it isn't right for you, you can still leave with that same severance.
- Anyone who wants a one-on-one with HR before deciding can have one.

Some details are still being worked out, including how the shift rotation will run. I'll share them as soon as they're settled, before anyone has to decide.

Closing a branch is hard for the people who built it and for the members who know you by name. Thank you for the work you've done there. I'm glad we're keeping every one of you.

Chief Operating Officer
</final_document>

Before you send it:

- **Your name:** The email signs off with your title only. Add your name above it.
- **The 14 affected staff:** If at all possible, tell them in person before this goes out. They shouldn't learn their branch is closing from an all-staff email. If you do meet with them first, you could add a line near the top saying you've already spoken with them.
- **Your commitment on details:** The line "before anyone has to decide" commits you to sharing the shift details before March 1. Keep it only if you can deliver that.
- **Not in the email:** I left out a severance cap, whether benefits continue, and what changes for the other five branches, because you don't know those yet. Expect questions on all three, especially the cap and benefits from the 14.
